title: Resolve the reader's text architecture
roadmap_anchor: Q1 > Debt > Resolve the reader's text architecture
acceptance: A written decision: keep one UITextView per block, or move to a single TextKit 2 view with viewport layout
The decision addresses long documents, VoiceOver reading order, Mac, and highlighting
Recorded in ROADMAP.md so it stops being a standing risk
notes: DECIDED 2026-08-25 by the overseer under delegated authority: KEEP one UITextView per block. Rationale, in order of weight: (1) Highlights persist as (blockIndex, start, length) and sync via CloudKit — per-block views make that anchoring native, where TextKit 2 needs a computed block-to-document-offset mapping layer to preserve the same stored records. (2) Blocks are heterogeneous: images, dividers, code, and bulleted lists are views, not runs of text; a single text view needs an attachment strategy for each. (3) LazyVStack virtualises very long documents for free. (4) Position restore keys off block id, which survives font-size changes in a way pixel offsets do not. (5) Mac does not force the change — either architecture needs a platform text view. ACCEPTED COST: no selection across block boundaries. NAMED FAILURE CONDITION: if T-0013 finds VoiceOver reading order or rotor navigation is bad across many small text views, this decision is wrong and must be revisited before the Mac app — that is the one piece of evidence that would overturn it. NOT decided on profiling data: T-0001 was never run, so the CPU question stays open and is orthogonal to this structural call.

history.detail: keep per-block UITextView; failure condition recorded
